item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Sewickley Academy rolls to PIAA girls soccer first round win over Conemaugh Township
item.description: OHIO TWP. — Following its first WPIAL championship in over 20 years, Sewickley Academy didn’t experience any championship hangover, with the team cruising to a 3-0 victory in the opening round of the PIAA Class 1A girls soccer championship on Tuesday, Nov. 10. “I’ve been around long enough to experience that championship hangover and it was something we talked about for a little bit, but the group responded very well and has a lot of experience,” Sewickley Academy head coach Gary Weber said. “The older players set a great tone for the younger ones, so it makes it a lot easier to coach.” Sewickley Academy (20-0) wasted little time to jump on Conemaugh Township, with forward Emma Eannarino taking the match into her own hands, putting up a hat trick in the first half to give the team a comfortable lead. The senior’s first goal came less than a minute into the contest, with Eannarino firing a shot off a Conemaugh Township (14-4) defender and into the back of the net. Eannarino’s second tally came just over 20 minutes after her first, sending a strong shot past the Conemaugh Township keeper to double Sewickley Academy’s lead. I have a lot of great teammates in the attack that help set up those opportunities,” Eannarino said. “We were back to our normal formation tonight, so it felt like a comfortable routine for all of us and our chemistry was back.” For the second straight game, it was another clean sheet for Sewickley Academy goalkeeper Courtney Weinreich, who after fending off several shots in the WPIAL championship against Winchester Thurston, had a relatively easy night in net while making a couple of easy saves. The Panthers’ back line allowed just one corner kick for Conemaugh Township in 80 minutes of action. “Amelia [Hayden] is who it all focuses on; she runs the show back there and holds the spot in the midfield,” Weber said. “She wins a lot of balls, calm, collected and finds balls to play through. item.title: Xavier improves to 3-0 ahead of litmus test against Mississippi State
item.description: Xavier men's basketball has spent the first eight days of the season building momentum. The Musketeers have overwhelmed Mount St. Mary's , leaned on their defense to pull away from Eastern Michigan and delivered another dominant performance Tuesday, Nov. 10 in defeating Detroit Mercy, 100-55, to move to 3-0. Three games, three wins, three blowouts with an average margin of victory of 37.7 points. Xavier couldn't have asked for a much better start to the season, even if the competition hasn't exactly a provided a glimpse of what the Musketeers might look like against the nation's best. More: Xavier University announces Richard Pitino bobblehead giveaway More: Richard Pitino provides injury updates on Appelhans, Elson Xavier put the finishing touches on an unblemished season-opening homestand Tuesday against the visiting Detroit Mercy Titans at Cintas Center. Xavier was a 35.5-point favorite against a Detroit Mercy squad that lost by 6 to Marquette in its season-opener. Xavier performed like a team should against one of the worst opponents on its schedule. The Musketeers took a 10-0 lead after just 89 seconds, prompting a Detroit timeout. Despite another first-half offensive lull, Xavier's commanding lead was never threatened with Detroit shooting 18.8% over the opening 20 minutes. The Titans started 2-for-21. Xavier was led by center Mike Nwoko with 17 points on 8 of 9 shooting. Guards Kalek House (16), Tru Washington (14) and Chance Westry (13) were also in double figures. Eleven different Musketeers made a field goal as Xavier shot over 50% from the field despite a sub-par night from distance (8-for-35). Defensively, Xavier held a third straight opponent under 55 points. The Musketeers grabbed 50-plus rebounds for the second time in three games, winning on the glass, 52-37. The early results have been encouraging, but the level of competition is about to take a significant jump. Four of Xavier's next five contests are against high-major opponents, beginning with a neutral site tilt on Friday, Nov. 13 against Mississippi State (3-0) in the Greenbrier Tip-Off in West Virginia. Xavier will then return to Cintas Center to host Cleveland State Nov. 17, then the Iowa Hawkeyes are in town on Friday, Nov. 20. The Musketeers will then face Texas A&M (Nov. 25) and No. 6 Virginia (Nov. 27) in the Battle 4 Atlantis in Nassau, Bahamas. item.title: Inside TKO's Saudi Arabia crisis: UFC, WWE workers speak out as safety fears escalate — 'Everyone just can't believe this'
item.description: The parent company of the WWE and UFC continues to plow forward with events in Saudi Arabia despite the ongoing military conflict there, but not all those within the company are happy about it. Sources tell Uncrowned that many people employed by TKO Group Holdings, Inc. are increasingly frustrated at the company's insistence on going through with events in Riyadh, the capital city of Saudi Arabia, even as the country continues to suffer ongoing missile and drone attacks by the Houthi militia in Yemen. One such attack took place in Riyadh's financial district just hours after WWE's Crown Jewel event concluded nearby on Saturday. While all WWE wrestlers were said to have left the country by the time a missile struck a tower owned by the state-run Aramco oil company on Sunday , some TKO workers said they felt that their safety has been little more than an afterthought as these events have gone on. "Why are you still even having these shows at this point?" said one source within the company who spoke on the condition of anonymity due to fear of reprisal. "I think the answer is, if they chose not to do the show, they would lose out on millions and millions of dollars. "From what I've heard, if we don't do the shows in Saudi Arabia or [United Arab Emirate] or Doha or wherever we are going, then our fourth quarter earnings will be off and our shareholders aren't going to get their money," the source continued. "So it's all about greed. They don't care about anybody's well-being. The level of greed with this company is so gross." Uncrowned reached out to TKO representatives for comment regarding the safety concerns expressed by employees in this story and the company's decision to proceed with events in Saudi Arabia. TKO had not responded at the time of publication. Saudi Arabia has been under continous attack since early October. Anadolu via Getty Images Multiple events under the TKO banner have been slated for Saudi Arabia this fall, despite the intensifying conflict on both sides of Saudi Arabia's border with Yemen. After attacks ramped up throughout the month of October — including a cruise missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Oct. 10, which killed 13 people and wounded over 300 more — the U.S. State Department ordered all diplomats and non-emergency government personnel to leave Saudi Arabia , citing security concerns. Other sports events set to take place in the country, including the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament and the PIF Saudi International golf tournament, have been postponed in light of the attacks. Fight sports, however, have continued ahead as planned. One prominent recent example was boxer Saul "Canelo" Alvarez's title bout with Christian Mbili on Oct. 31 . That fight took place in Riyadh despite a "hostile aerial threat" warning issued by the Saudi Arabian government just two days prior to the event. item.title: ‘A bit alarming’: Joel Klatt says Jeremiah Smith ‘didn’t even play great football’ in loss to Oregon
item.description: Sep 19, 2026; Columbus, Ohio, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) runs after making the catch during the first quarter against the Kent State Golden Flashes at Ohio Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Jeremiah Smith’s frustration during Ohio State’s loss to Oregon has been one of the biggest storylines of the week. Most of the conversation has centered on how little the Buckeyes got the ball to their superstar receiver. But Joel Klatt thinks there’s plenty of blame to go around, including for Smith himself. The FOX analyst said that Smith “didn’t even play great football” against the Ducks, calling what he saw on film from the star receiver “a bit alarming.” Smith’s Frustration Ohio State jumped out to a 14-0 lead against Oregon on Saturday before the Ducks scored 38 straight points on their way to a 41-28 win. Smith went more than two full quarters without a catch, and late in the third quarter, he was seen screaming toward the sideline . Smith finished with seven catches for 133 yards and a touchdown, but much of that came after the game was out of reach. Columbus radio host Jeremy Birmingham called him “a petulant child” for the outburst, while Urban Meyer came to his defense , calling Smith “the perfect teammate.” Klatt, meanwhile, ripped Ohio State’s game plan for Smith after the loss to USC, saying that it “can’t be your game plan” for a player of his caliber. ‘A bit alarming’ On the most recent episode of The Joel Klatt Show , Klatt said that everyone at Ohio State shares the blame for the loss, and that includes Smith. “Even Jeremiah Smith, and I know, trust me, I’m going to get to their lack of usage of Jeremiah Smith,” Klatt said. “However, the film suggests that everybody shares in this. Jeremiah didn’t even play great football. Now, I know that he put up some numbers. There’s no doubt.” “Even Jeremiah didn’t play great all game. There were times when he was slow off the line of scrimmage. He didn’t win the one-on-one ball down into the end zone early in the game,” Klatt continued. “He was late out of his breaks. There were times when the routes weren’t being run, I’ll be honest, full speed. And that was a bit alarming to see for me, cause I’ve come to see a standard on film from number four at Ohio State that is higher than what was on film on Saturday’s game.” Klatt did say that he understood Smith’s frustration, and he put much of it on the scheme. “I have covered this team more than any other team in my career, and I have been around Jeremiah a lot, and this is not him, and I think that that frustration was layered,” Klatt said. Klatt added that “there was virtually no creativity with Jeremiah Smith, how to get him the ball in specific ways. item.title: WTGL debut match draws nearly 100,000 viewers going against NFL
item.description: WTGL had plenty of competition for its Nov. 8 debut, going up against the NFL, the men's golf World Wide Technology Championship televised by Golf Channel and NASCAR. The match, televised by ESPN, drew an average of 97,000 viewers at SoFi Center, peaking at 138,000. The WWT, which featured a playoff between Blades Brown and Ben James, had an average viewership of 110,00. Brown and James are playing this season for TGL. WTGL's inaugural match — in which Los Angeles Golf Club defeated New York Golf Club , 3-1 — delivered the third highest women’s golf telecast out of 24 events since the Sept. 13 Solheim Cup . The league's second match, Tuesday, Nov. 10, was televised by ION. The WTGL format follows TGL, the men's version co-founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy, that is entering its third year. The initial match was a success with the players. "Witnessing LPGA players and LPGA stars in this format is so different," said LA's Michelle Wie West. "We have such amazing players and personalities out on Tour, and it's really cool that every single shot you see so many statistics on the screen. I think that's something that's missing from our normal broadcast. I think for two hours, LPGA fans, existing fans, can witness our players in a whole different light, and I think we'll attract new fans as well too." The Minnesota Vikings traded for Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders to help improve the quarterback situation that had been holding back the offense through the first half of the regular season. While nearly every sports fan is on board that Cousins is an upgrade over previous starter Kyler Murray , Skip Bayless went full Skip Bayless on Tuesday and offered a take that you won’t believe. Bayless posted a clip on social media claiming that he believes Murray is a better quarterback than Cousins right now. The 74-year-old sports analyst said he chose the Vikings to win the NFC North at the beginning of the campaign, but that Murray was one of the reasons why. He goes on to explain that he is dumbfounded that the organization decided to trade for Cousins and effectively move on from Murray. “My mind is on Minneapolis and the move the Vikings just made,” Bayless said… “I did pick the Vikings to win the North. I’m hanging in with it as they fall to 6-2. The two reasons I picked the Vikings were obviously: No. 1, the defense, and No. 2, Kyler Murray. I remain a big Kyler fan… And I’m amused and shell-shocked over the new narrative he’s too little… Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I think the Vikings’ ceiling would have been higher with Kyler Murray, because he’s been playing pretty well the last three games,” Bayless continued… “I don’t hate the Kirk Cousins move, only because he’s been there, done that… He’s obviously better than Carson Wentz… But in the end, I don’t know why they gave up so quickly on Kyler for Kirk Cousins.” Kyler>>>>>>Cousins pic.twitter.com/j90VRvc7qE — Skip Bayless (@RealSkipBayless) November 10, 2026 Bayless went on to claim that he still thinks the Vikings will reach the playoffs with the 38-year-old commanding the huddle. item.title: Bath volleyball eyes historic regional title after semifinal sweep
item.description: BATH — A year ago, Kyria Pairolero and the Bath volleyball team accomplished all it listed on its preseason goal sheet. They won a tournament and also captured a district championship among other things during a successful 2025 season. With a team full of returners, Bath has made it a point to accomplish more this year. "We took every single one of those goals that we had last year and set them up a notch," Pairolero said. "It wasn't win a tournament, it was win three tournaments. It was like this kind of stuff." The Bees have accomplished much of what they set out to do in what has turned out to be a special season that has included CMAC regular season and tournament titles and a district championship. Bath has more it wants to achieve and took a step toward its bid to make history by sweeping Marlette in three sets by scores of 25-13, 25-17 and 25-22 in a Division 3 regional semifinal on its home floor Tuesday, Nov. 10. The win sends the Bees into a regional final against Leslie on Thursday, Nov. 12. "They are just a really highly motivated group of kids," Bath coach Madison Margraves-Beukema said. "They really are kind of chasing after the same goals. We've been working towards a long list of goals this year. One of them is to make history at our school. We've never had a regional championship at our school. They are just really, really motivated to try to do that. We're really glad to get to move on to the next day." A year ago the Bees had their postseason run halted by Reese in a regional semifinal in what was their first appearance in the second stage of the MHSAA state tournament since 2020. Now after Tuesday's win Bath has matched the state tournament run made by the 2018 squad coached by Kristen McIntyre that reached the regional final before being eliminated. More: MHSAA volleyball: See the Greater Lansing regional pairings, results Pairolero and teammates now want to have a different outcome than that group and aim to build on a special season that included the Bees not dropping a set in CMAC play through the regular season and postseason tournament. Bath also hasn't dropped a set yet in the state tournament and overcame a 22-19 deficit in the third set to wrap up its regional semifinal victory. "Most of us are returning players so I feel like we all just kind of had a bone to pick," Pairolero said. "We wanted to get back to this place. That was one of our first goals. I know that was my goal. We really, really wanted to work hard and our goal was to stay undefeated at home so this is just another step." Leslie reached the regional final with a sweep of Burton Atherton, winning each game by a 25-10 score. item.title: LSU Soccer Falls to Alabama in the Quarterfinals of the SEC Tournament
item.description: No. 11-seeded LSU fell to No. 3-seeded Alabama, 2-1, in the quarterfinals of the SEC Tournament on Tuesday afternoon at the Ashton Brosnaham Soccer Complex, per an official press release. Despite a strong first-half performance from goalkeeper Audur Scheving, who recorded five saves in the opening 45 minutes, the Tigers and Crimson Tide entered halftime scoreless. Alabama outshot LSU 9-2 in the first half, but Scheving’s efforts kept the match level heading into the break. LSU increased its offensive pressure in the second half, recording 11 shots compared to just two in the opening period. However, Alabama struck first in the 69th minute when Melina Rebimbas found the back of the net off assists from Soph Martelli and Kennedy Garcia to give the Crimson Tide a 1-0 advantage. The Tigers responded in the 80th minute when Ava Galligan scored her eighth goal of the season to even the match at 1-1. The equalizer came following a pair of blocked shots from Emma Alvord, giving LSU momentum with just over 10 minutes remaining. Alabama regained the lead in the 87th minute when Ashley Roni converted a penalty kick to put the Crimson Tide ahead, 2-1. Despite LSU’s late offensive efforts, Alabama held on to secure the victory and advance to the SEC Tournament semifinals. Scheving finished the match with seven saves, while Galligan led the Tigers with three shots and one goal. LSU recorded 13 total shots, including 11 in the second half, while Alabama finished with 20 shots.

item.title: A lockout is coming and the Dodgers don't care
item.description: Mar 30, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers general manager and executive vice president Brandon Gomes watches batting practice before the game against the Cleveland Guardians at Dodger Stadium. LAS VEGAS — Brandon Gomes tried to watch the World Series. He made it through a couple of games. "I tried to watch the first couple games, and then after that, I was like, this is personally too painful," the Dodgers general manager said Tuesday at the GM meetings. "I think I'll just check the box score afterwards." It's hard to blame him. The Dodgers were trying to become the first team in a quarter-century to win three straight World Series titles. Instead, the Milwaukee Brewers swept them in the National League Championship Series, a year after the Dodgers had swept Milwaukee in the same round and then beat Tampa Bay for the first championship in franchise history. Asked whether it took any sting away that the team that knocked them out went on to win it all, Gomes didn't hesitate. "No, it doesn't take any sting away," he said. "You just don't feel good if you don't win." That's the part of the Dodgers that should worry the rest of baseball. Two championships didn't make losing any easier for them. If anything, it made it worse. And while most of the sport spent this week in Las Vegas bracing for a lockout when the collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, the Dodgers sounded like a team that hasn't changed a thing. "For us, we're totally focused, business as usual," Gomes said, "Trying to make sure we're as prepared as possible in case things happen in different ways, whether that's a trade or free agency." That's not a slogan. It's how the Dodgers have operated since Guggenheim bought the team, and nothing about a work stoppage or a salary cap proposal is going to change it. Gomes was asked about salary cap proposals that would put the Dodgers well over the line before they sign a single new player. He shrugged it off. "I think the biggest thing is we're going to function like we always do," Gomes said, "and whatever it is, it is, and we'll figure it out." Asked for his best guess on when opening day will be, he laughed. "I don't even know what opening day schedule is right now," he said. Every other front office in Las Vegas is trying to figure out how to plan for a season that may not start on time under rules that don't exist yet. The Dodgers are planning to be the best team in baseball whenever it starts, and the oddsmakers agree. item.title: Habs fans give Carey Price a 4 minute standing ovation
item.description: Habs fans give Carey Price a 4 minute standing ovation There are certain moments in hockey that transcend the sport itself, moments where the game takes a backseat and the bond between a city and a player becomes the main event. Tuesday night at the Bell Centre was one of those moments. Fresh off his Hockey Hall of Fame induction in Toronto just a day earlier, Carey Price returned to the building he called home for 15 years, and the fans of the Montreal Canadiens made sure he knew exactly what he meant to them. The crowd erupted into a standing ovation that lasted nearly four minutes, filling the arena with a deafening blend of "Ca-rey! Ca-rey!" chants and the iconic "Olé, Olé" that has become synonymous with big nights in Montreal. Price stood near the team benches, next to the five individual trophies he earned during his illustrious career, visibly moved and fighting back tears as he tried to address the crowd. https://x.com/NHL/status/2120309739649417635 "You gave me a home for 15 years. It was an honor to be your goalie," Price told the packed arena, his voice trembling with emotion. He closed with a heartfelt message that captured the moment perfectly: "From the bottom of my heart, the most sincere 'Merci beaucoup.'" A Career Worth Celebrating Price's path to the Hockey Hall of Fame is one of the most remarkable stories in the sport. Growing up in the remote community of Anahim Lake, British Columbia, his father Jerry would fly him in a four-seat plane 320 kilometres to Williams Lake three times a week just so the young goaltender could play minor hockey. That dedication paid off when the Canadiens selected him fifth overall in the 2005 draft, beginning a 15-year relationship that would see Price become the franchise's all-time leader in wins. Over 712 regular season games, Price compiled a record of 361-261-79 with a 2.51 goals-against average, a .917 save percentage, and 49 shutouts. He backstopped Canada to Olympic gold in 2014 and swept the Hart Trophy and Vezina Trophy in 2015 after posting a staggering .933 save percentage across 66 games. A member of the Ulkatcho First Nation, Price became known for his exceptional positioning, his calm demeanor under pressure, and those highlight-reel windmill glove saves that made fans hold their breath. Perhaps the most bittersweet chapter of his career came in 2021, when he carried an underdog Canadiens squad all the way to the Stanley Cup Final against the Tampa Bay Lightning. He never did hoist the Cup, and a degenerative knee injury limited him to just five more appearances after that magical run. His final game came on April 29, 2022, a 10-2 victory over Florida at the Bell Centre, though fans didn't know at the time they were watching him play for the last time. item.title: Lakers Shake Up Roster, Bring in New Center Amid Frontcourt Depth Concerns
item.description: Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google The Los Angeles Lakers shuffled the fringes of their roster, moving out center Lawson Lovering, who was taking a two-way spot, in favor of center Carson Cooper. The Lakers signed Cooper to a two-way contract after he appeared in one game for the Memphis Grizzlies before being waived. Cooper was on a two-way deal with Memphis, and now he joins the Lakers on the same deal. He spent four years in college, finishing off his career with a senior year at Michigan State, where he averaged averaging 11.1 points on 58.4% shooting, 7.1 rebounds, 1.5 assists, and 1.0 blocks in 26.8 minutes. Mandatory Credit: Ed Szczepanski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Cooper appeared in 137 college games. Lovering, meanwhile, inked a two-way deal in late October, with the Lakers hoping the big man would show something as a backup center. However, he just got garbage time run with LA, appearing in two games. Why the Lakers really need a back-up center Right now, the Lakers have Walker Kessler taking most of the minutes at center, averaging 30+ minutes per game, with the rest going to either Sandro Mamukelashvili or Jarred Vanderbilt at the small-ball five. Against teams without two standout big men, the Lakers can succeed in those matchups. However, if Kessler is off the floor and a big body is on the floor, it is tough for the Lakers to survive in certain matchups. Lovering failed to stick, but head coach JJ Redick will hope Cooper can help ease the need for a big man. Luka Doncic really thrives with a quality big man, and he can make them play better than their actual level because he makes the game easy for them. Cooper doesn’t have a high bar to clear, and if he stays around, his game can really come together.
